## What session 8 is for {.scrollable}
::::: columns

:::: {.column width="33%"}

### The mathematics

- State the **Bayes classifier** and say why no rule can beat it
- Find nearest neighbours **by hand** from a Euclidean distance
- Decompose test error into **squared bias, variance and irreducible error**
- Say what happens to KNN as the number of predictors grows

::::

:::: {.column width="33%"}

### The Python

- Standardise, split, and choose $k$ by cross-validation
- Measure a classifier with **AUC** rather than accuracy alone
- Fit the simple alternative too, and let it win if it does

::::

:::: {.column width="33%"}

### The international business

- Classify firms or countries when you have no theory of the boundary
- Say why a flexible method that scores 0.51 has told you something
- Justify complexity against a simpler model that was actually fitted

::::

:::::

## 1 · Reproduce — 20 min {.scrollable}

**Bluwstein, Buckmann, Joseph, Kapadia & Şimşek (2023)**: can credit growth and the yield curve
predict a banking crisis — and does a flexible model beat a logit? Part 1 of the script:

```python
import pandas as pd

SITE = "https://warint.github.io/quantitative-methods/data/"
jst = pd.read_csv(SITE + "session-08/jst_crises.csv")   # 18 economies, 1870-2020

# outcome: a crisis starts within two years · train 1870-1979, test 1980-2020
# -> logit, KNN (K by cross-validation) and a random forest, scored by test AUC
# -> which predictors matter: permutation importance
```

::: {.check}
A failed reproduction that you **diagnose** teaches as much as one that works. One you do not attempt teaches nothing.
Does your ranking of predictors match the paper's? Does the flexible model win, as it does there?
:::

::: {.muted}
"It did not work" is not a diagnosis. Where did it stop, and what did you check?
:::

## 2 · Apply to your own angle — 35 min {.scrollable}

Part 2 of the script — after you set `MY_ANGLE`:

```python
core = pd.read_csv(SITE + "core.csv")            # shared: falling_behind_next is the outcome
mine = pd.read_csv(SITE + MY_ANGLE + ".csv")     # your angle
mine = mine.groupby(["geo", "time"]).mean(numeric_only=True).reset_index()  # one row per country-year
df   = core.merge(mine, on=["geo", "time"], how="inner")
```

Then the same comparison — logit against KNN, $K$ by cross-validation, AUC on the last two years.
Replace the default predictor list with the ones **your question** needs.

::: {.warn}
A number without units is not a finding — and an AUC without its benchmark (0.5, and the logit) is not one either.
:::

## 3 · Break one assumption — 15 min

Every method in this course rests on something.

::: {.step}
Find the assumption this one leans on hardest. Break it **deliberately**. Record what happened to
your answer. Part 3 of the script has three ready to run: **(a)** no standardising, **(b)** fewer
predictors, **(c)** a random split instead of a time split.
:::

::: {.check}
This is the part that matters most. A group that shows how its result falls apart understands
it; a group that only shows it holding does not yet know.
:::

## 4 · Write it down — 20 min

250 words, in a file in your own folder — it is what you report from:

::: {.tight}
- What you found, **in units**
- Which assumption you broke, and what it did
- What this result does **not** license you to claim
:::

::: {.muted}
And the standing rule: one LLM output you identified as wrong, and how you established that.
:::

## The usual mistakes

::: {.tight}
- Running KNN on unstandardised predictors
- Choosing $k$ on the test set
- Reporting accuracy with no benchmark
- Treating a low training error as evidence of anything
:::

::: {.warn}
And everywhere in this course: an association described in causal language.
:::

## Two-minute report

| | |
|---|---|
| **One number** | with its units and its uncertainty |
| **One assumption** | the one you broke, and what happened |
| **One limit** | what you cannot claim from this |

::: {.muted}
Listen for traceable evidence, not confidence of delivery.
:::
